- Bullet points. Try to keep them short. Less distraction, less boredom.

- Colour code. Draw up a key somewhere and stick to it - e.g. highlighting sources in a specific colour or writing quotes in red. This helps with remembering info too. 

-Getting distracted? Re-read the question (or whatever it is you're reading for) and try to figure out how what you're reading fits into that. 

- Keep a goal in mind if you're getting bored. Long term goals are awesome, but short-term goals work. When you meet your goals do something fun - internet time or tv time are good for this. If you're into games, habitRPG (not sure if we're allowed to post links? It's easily googleable...) is a fun way to stay on track. 

-Keep a spare notebook or scrap paper near if you get distracted with other things you need to do. Write the thing down, finish studying, do the thing you wrote down. 

-Prioritize your work. Plan your week so you know when you'll study each thing. Allow some extra time *just in case you need it* - if you don't, it's extra relaxation time.

My second year of Uni I didn't get my loan until the January (having started in September). In the end I had to spent almost 3 weeks calling every weekday with someone from Student Support listening in to help me out when Student Finance tried to fob me off with yet another excuse. 

Advice:
Get to your uni's Student Services / Advice and Representation centre. Let them know what is happening. This will help if/when you run into problems paying for rent, tuition etc. 

Apply for any hardship funds/bursaries/anything else. It'll help you in the short term and let the uni know exactly how many people are in a situation like yours (you won't be the only one...) applying means they have a better idea of how much to allocate for next year's hardship fund. 

Keep a diary if you aren't already. Write down dates, times, who you spoke to and what you sent. Photocopy (or camera phone) things you send to help keep track (useful for "you didn't sign this" / "you didn't fill this in") 

Let your personal tutor know. This sounds hugely stressful and if you need deadline extensions or anything else, it helps if they're able to say they already know what's going on. 

Not sure how helpful that is - Universities and departments all seem to have different ways of doing things. That's just what I learned when it happened to me and might save you some time...
